qnas.question: Describe the transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block: anatomical basis, ultrasound-guided technique, indications, and complications.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.body_md: The TAP block is a fascial plane block depositing local anaesthetic between internal oblique and transversus abdominis, anaesthetising the anterior rami of T6-L1.

sections.heading: Anatomical basis
sections.body_md: Three muscle layers form the anterolateral abdominal wall: external oblique, internal oblique, transversus abdominis. The neurovascular plane lies between the latter two.

sections.heading: Technique - USG-guided
sections.body_md: High-frequency linear probe in the mid-axillary line between costal margin and iliac crest; identify the three layers; in-plane needle to the fascial plane; hydrodissect; deposit 15-20 ml per side.

sections.heading: Indications
sections.body_md: Analgesia for lower abdominal surgery: caesarean section, appendicectomy, inguinal hernia repair, abdominoplasty.

sections.heading: Complications
sections.body_md: Intraperitoneal injection, bowel puncture, liver laceration (right-sided), local anaesthetic systemic toxicity, block failure.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body_md: A landmark-simple, ultrasound-reliable analgesic block of the abdominal wall; know the plane, the volume, and the LAST risk.

images.content_description: Ultrasound cross-section of the abdominal wall showing external oblique, internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscle layers with the needle tip and local anaesthetic spread in the transversus abdominis plane

qnas.question: Outline the difficult airway algorithm for an anticipated difficult intubation.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.body_md: A clinical situation in which a trained anaesthesiologist experiences difficulty with facemask ventilation, laryngoscopy, or both.

sections.heading: Assessment
sections.body_md: History, Mallampati, thyromental distance, mouth opening, neck mobility; plan awake techniques when two or more predictors align.

sections.heading: Plan A-D
sections.body_md: Plan A optimal laryngoscopy; Plan B supraglottic airway; Plan C facemask oxygenation and wake-up; Plan D front-of-neck access.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body_md: Declare difficulty early; prioritise oxygenation over intubation at every branch.

qnas.question: Describe rapid sequence induction: indications, drugs, and technique.

sections.heading: Indications
sections.body_md: Full stomach, emergency surgery, gastro-oesophageal reflux, pregnancy beyond the first trimester.

sections.heading: Technique
sections.body_md: Preoxygenation 3 minutes; induction agent + rapid-onset relaxant; cricoid pressure; no mask ventilation; intubate and confirm with capnography.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body_md: Speed and aspiration prophylaxis are the whole point; have suction and a rescue plan ready.
